The prophets no longer present God’s will or proclaim His commandment, but for temporal honor, pleasures and material gain they deceive souls with smooth, false words and partiality. They are no longer messengers of heaven and ambassadors of God, but have become like the enemy of good, the erring deceiver; there is no place for truth in them; they have become traitors and treacherous, so that no one trusts them. As the Lord says through Jeremiah: “Behold, I am against the prophets, saith the LORD, that use their tongues, and say, He saith. Behold, I am against them that prophesy false dreams, saith the LORD, and do tell them, and cause my people to err by their lies, and by their lightness; yet I sent them not, nor commanded them: therefore they shall not profit this people at all, saith the LORD” (Jer 23:32).

Thus the false prophets went astray and led the people astray, speaking what was from themselves and ascribing it to God. As for the priests, instead of serving in the temple for the sanctification of the people, they themselves became the cause of defilement of the sanctuary or the temple. And instead of teaching by the Law and the divine commandment, so that the people might return to God by repentance and obedience, they themselves became transgressors of the Law. The priests betrayed the divine covenant, corrupted worship, and shaped the divine word according to their own desires, to serve themselves and to flatter the great and the rich.
The just LORD is in the midst thereof; he will not do iniquity.
Every morning doth he bring his judgment to light, he faileth not.

entries.section: C. Concerning injustice it was said:

paragraphs.text: But the unjust knoweth no shame. [5]

The Jews thought that the secret of their sanctification, their success and their victory over the nations was the presence of Jerusalem, the city of God, and the establishment of worship in the temple of Solomon. Truly God is present, but not to overshadow them with the wings of His tenderness and mercy; rather to look and to carry out His divine justice, disciplining His people for the corruption that had come upon them, without a desire to return to Him and repent of the corruption. It is as though He says: You boast that God is in your midst. Be it so; for He is just, so why are you not just like Him? He is light, so why do you practice the works of darkness and do evil as if in secret, as though God does not see you, nor hear your words, nor perceive your thoughts?

The presence of the holy God in your midst does not justify you, but on the contrary condemns you for your corruption. “For the LORD thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp, to deliver thee, and to give up thine enemies before thee; therefore shall thy camp be holy: that he see no unclean thing in thee, and turn away from thee” (Deut 23:14). “Say unto them, Ye shall be holy: for I the LORD your God am holy” (Lev 19:2). “Yet will they lean upon the LORD, and say, Is not the LORD among us? none evil can come upon us” (Mic 3:11).

“Every morning doth he bring his judgment to light”; if God in His long-suffering has not yet disciplined, yet with every new morning let them expect God’s judgment in the light, that is, openly, where He disciplines and no one can justify himself or resist the discipline and flee from it. It is not impossible for Him to carry out His judgments.

Repentant souls say with the prophet Jeremiah: “His mercies fail not; they are new every morning” (Lam 3:22-23), but the obstinate must expect divine discipline every morning. If God threatens the careless and heedless sinners that the day of discipline is coming swiftly, He does not desire the grief and bitterness of men; rather, in threatening, He only opens the door that they may enjoy His surpassing mercies through their repentance.

* “Upon the wicked he shall rain snares” (Ps 11:6). Without any doubt it is the Lord who prepares snares for the sinners themselves, that He may catch those who have misused their freedom, and drive them to walk in the straight way under His bridle, making it within their power to advance with Him who says: “I am the way” (Jn 14:6). Therefore in Jeremiah (Jer 16:16) the Lord sends fishers and hunters to set their nets for the fish that are lost amid the whirlpools, and to catch the beasts that roam on the mountains and hills, that we may enjoy salvation… For this passage and what follows does not promise repentance to sinners, as many believe, but rather presents a promise of healing.
St. Jerome I have cut off the nations.
Their towers are desolate.
I made their streets waste, that none passeth by.

entries.section: C. Concerning injustice it was said:

paragraphs.text: Their cities are destroyed, so that there is no man, that there is none inhabitant. [6]

It was fitting for the people of God to take warning from God’s disciplines of the surrounding pagan nations, for He was long-suffering with them, but at the appointed time they fell under His very firm judgments, until kingdoms vanished, the palaces of their kings were struck, their great cities were destroyed, and they were turned into a wasteland without inhabitant.

Perhaps he means here the seven nations of Canaan mentioned in Leviticus (Lev 18:28), or the nations around them, whose destruction God permitted so that Jerusalem might take warning and Judah return to the Lord by repentance.
St. Jerome and many of the Fathers see that the nations that the Lord cuts off signify the heretics who preach false teachings, but they are quickly cut off.

* “O my God, make them like a wheel” (Ps 83:13), so that there is no stability in them, but they are always unsettled and have no firm position, always moving, rolling (like a wheel) backward and forward. For just as the wheel is not stable in itself, so the heretics do not remain firmly settled in their teachings and opinions, but always change them.

* They do not seek knowledge for salvation, but seek a new teaching in order to overcome the adversary. Let them fall by their many conflicting opinions, and let them have one refuge, which is You, O my God!
St. Jerome I said, Surely thou wilt fear me.
Thou wilt receive instruction; so their dwelling should not be cut off, howsoever I punished them.

entries.section: C. Concerning injustice it was said:

paragraphs.text: But they rose early, and corrupted all their doings. [7]

God speaks with us in our language, as He presented to His people the example of the surrounding nations, expecting them to bear His fear, accept His discipline and return to Him, so that the ruin of which He spoke would not come upon them. For even while threatening them with ruin He desires that they not fall into it, but be saved from it. He threatened through the prophets that He would cut off the dwelling from them or remove it from Jerusalem, but by His threat He desires not to remove it if they return to Him.

By saying “their dwelling” He ascribes the temple to Jerusalem or to the people, not to Himself, for He did not say “My dwelling.” This is God’s manner in dealing with His people. If they are sanctified, He counts them His people and calls their feasts His feasts, their Sabbaths His Sabbaths, and their temple His temple; and if they are not sanctified, He does not count them His people, nor His feasts, nor His Sabbaths, nor His city, nor His temple.

What grieves His heart is that while He expects them to heed what happened to their neighbors, so that they repent and return to Him, behold, in obstinacy they rise early in order to provoke God by corrupting all their doings. They strove all the more to search for an early time in which to practice every defilement and uncleanness.

The remarkable thing about man, whether at the level of the individual or the community, is that he wants God to be long-suffering with him and vengeful toward those who oppose him. The Jewish people used to ask for vengeance on the pagan peoples who opposed them, while at the same time they themselves committed the very evils of the nations and fell into idol worship and the abomination of the nations, expecting God’s long-suffering toward them.

“Lord, how long shall the sinners, how long shall the sinners boast?” (Ps 94:3) In lack of long-suffering, mankind does not want God to be long-suffering with others. As creatures we truly wish to be objects of compassion, so we ask God for long-suffering toward us, and that He not be long-suffering toward our enemies. When we sin we beseech God to be long-suffering with us, but when someone sins against us, why do we not expect God’s long-suffering toward him?

St. Jerome * You complain because the wicked are not punished (now); do not complain lest you be punished with them. This man has committed theft and lives; you complain against God because the one who committed theft against you has not died… If you want the hand of another corrected (so that he does not steal), correct your own tongues. You want the heart of another man corrected (so that he does not rob you); correct your own hearts toward God, lest while you desire God’s vengeance, it comes and finds you first. For He will come, He will come and judge those who persist in their evil, who despise His long-suffering and the extent of His mercy, so that you treasure up for yourselves wrath against the day of wrath.
St. Augustine

entries.section: 2. All falling under indignation:

paragraphs.text: Therefore wait ye upon me, saith the LORD.
Until the day that I rise up to the prey: for my determination is to gather the nations, that I may assemble the kingdoms, to pour upon them mine indignation, even all my fierce anger.
For all the earth shall be devoured with the fire of my jealousy. [8]

It is as though God looks to the very few holy ones of His people to speak to them of His plan even in the moments of His wrath. He asks them to look to the coming times of glory. For after the day of punishment or discipline comes upon all the nations, His jealousy devours all the earth, that He may establish His heavenly Kingdom. For in His jealousy He does not seek the destruction of people, but the destruction of what is earthly in them, that they may become a holy temple for Him, bearing holy heavenly traits.
“I rise up to the prey”: after the firm discipline the Lord carries off the spoils of victory when the nations return and believe in Him, and they become His joyful spoils.

entries.section: 3. The rising of the worshipping Jerusalem:

paragraphs.text: 9 For then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the LORD, to serve him with one shoulder. 10 From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia my suppliants, even the daughter of my dispersed, shall bring mine offering.
For then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the LORD, to serve him with one shoulder. [9]

As He removes from the nations what is earthly in order to give them of what is His own, what is heavenly, He removes from them what came upon mankind in the days of Noah, when He confused their tongues so that they might not build for themselves a tower whose top reached to heaven. Now He makes all the nations offer the sacrifice of prayer and praise with a pure lip (a pure language). What is this pure language but the language of the Spirit? In Christ Jesus the Church is gathered from the ends of the world to its ends, worshipping Him in a holy heavenly spirit, with one mind and one heart. This is what God announced through the prophets concerning the Church of the New Testament; we mention by way of example: “In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan” (Isa 19:18). “And the LORD shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall there be one LORD, and his name one” (Zech 14:9).
As all come to have one mind, all work together, bearing His easy or sweet yoke as with one shoulder; so all share in the work of His one cross with joy and gladness of heart!

* When the patience of the Jews was exhausted they could no longer bear (the praises of the children to the Lord Christ), and they tried to silence these children to whom the Lord referred in Isaiah: “Behold, I and the children whom the LORD hath given me” (Isa 8:18). Since the elders and the old men of the Jews were silent, and the Pharisees also, gnashing their teeth in envy full of malice, the children cried out and glorified Christ. For if they are silent, the very stones will cry out, that is, the nations of whom it is written in the Gospel: [The Lord is able to raise up from these stones sons to Abraham] (cf. Mt 3:9). These stones signify us, who at one time were hard of heart, and now believe in Christ Jesus, and have enjoyed sonship among the sons of Abraham, and have become sons of God Almighty, to whom be glory forever and ever, Amen.

St. Jerome * Since this text (Isa 11:6) does not refer literally to predatory animals, let the Jews say when this actually happens. For the wolf never feeds with a lamb. And if this were to happen, that they feed together, of what use would that be to the human race? The text refers not to predatory beasts but to a predatory people. It refers to the Scythians, the Thracians, the Mauritanians, the Indians, the Samaritans and the Persians. Another prophet has shown this clearly, that all these nations will come together under one yoke, and each one will worship Him in his place (Zeph 3:9; 2:11). He says that the people will no longer worship Him in Jerusalem, but in every place in the world. The people will no longer be commanded to go to Jerusalem, but each one will remain in his house and offer this worship.
St. John Chrysostom

entries.section: 3. The rising of the worshipping Jerusalem:

paragraphs.text: From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia my suppliants, even the daughter of my dispersed, shall bring mine offering. [10]

He refers here to a group of Jews who were scattered and went to Cush; therefore He calls them “my dispersed,” and they beseech God, awaiting return and reform. When these accept faith in the Lord Christ they offer the Lord’s spiritual offering (Rom 12:1) outside the land of Israel, as the Church of the New Testament.

Origen sees that as a man looks to Israel, that it will be saved by their accepting the faith after the fullness of the Gentiles has come in to the faith (Rom 11:25), the nations are gathered with Israel to worship God as under one yoke, with one shoulder (Zeph 3:9). And from the ends of Ethiopia (Cush) they offer Him sacrifices (Zeph 3:10), as it is said in the Psalms: [Ethiopia shall stretch out her hand to God, and to the kings of the earth] (cf. Ps 68:31-32).

St. Jerome often spoke of the holy people of God as the garment of majesty to which the Lord cleaves. He sees that the Lord has put on majesty (His people who enjoy the majesty of His grace), and that when He lost the first people the Lord did not remain naked, but made for Himself a garment from the nations.

* He says: “The LORD reigneth; let the earth rejoice; let the multitude of isles be glad thereof” (Ps 97:1). It is not one island that rejoices, that is, Judea, but many islands, that is, the whole world!

* His whole aim in ascending the Cross is to lift us up from the earth. I think that the Cross of the Savior is the ladder that Jacob saw. On that ladder the angels descend and ascend. And on that ladder, which is the Cross, the Jews were descending and the nations ascending.
St. Jerome

entries.section: 4. The humble Jerusalem:

paragraphs.text: 11 In that day shalt thou not be ashamed for all thy doings, wherein thou hast transgressed against me: for then I will take away out of the midst of thee them that rejoice in thy pride, and thou shalt no more be haughty because of my holy mountain. 12 I will also leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor people, and they shall trust in the name of the LORD.
In that day shalt thou not be ashamed for all thy doings, wherein thou hast transgressed against me.
For then I will take away out of the midst of thee them that rejoice in thy pride, and thou shalt no more be haughty because of my holy mountain. [11]

As He announces the radical reform by the raising up of the new Jerusalem and the appearance of the Church of the New Testament, she is no longer put to shame by an evil deed, for He removes the proud who boast of the blessings that belonged to the people of Israel in a literal, formal, deadly manner. What they thought to be the secret of their beauty, their pride in the temple of Solomon and in Jerusalem as the city of God, etc., has departed from Israel, and the inner beauty has been given to the believers, as He granted them His Holy Spirit.
This holy few are marked by the spirit of humility and do not accept pride.

* What then? Did they all perish and were they removed from the root of David and from the tribe of Judah? No, for some of this root believed, and indeed several thousand men of this stock believed, after the resurrection of the Lord. They were enraged and crucified Him, and afterward they began to see miracles done in the name of the Crucified. They were terrified when they saw such great power done in His name, He who was in their hands seemed unable to do it. So they were pricked in their hearts and finally believed that the divinity had been hidden in Him, whom they thought to be like other men. They asked counsel of the Apostles, and they answered them: “Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ” (Acts 2:38). Christ rose to judge those who crucified Him, and so He turned His presence from the Jews to the Gentiles; yet God seemed to be working for the remnant of Israel. And it was said to Him on their behalf: “For thy servant David’s sake turn not away the face of thine anointed” (Ps 132:10). If the straw is judged, let the wheat be gathered together. Let the remnant be saved, as Isaiah says: [The remnant shall be saved] (cf. Isa 10:21). From them came the twelve Apostles, and from them the five hundred brethren to whom the Lord showed Himself after His resurrection (1 Cor 15:6), and of them several thousand were baptized (Acts 2:41), who laid the price of their possessions at the feet of the Apostles. Thus was fulfilled the prayer that was offered here to God: “For thy servant David’s sake turn not away the face of thine anointed” (Ps 132:10).
St. Augustine

entries.section: 4. The humble Jerusalem:

paragraphs.text: I will also leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor people, and they shall trust in the name of the LORD. [12]
St. Augustine sees here a prophecy about Israel, who have become like the sand of the sea, that the remnant of them will be saved by their accepting faith in the Lord Christ.
As pride is removed from them and they practice humility, they trust in the Lord and rely on His work in them. Here he links true humility with living faith full of confidence in the work of God.

* In some of those who crucified Christ miracles were accomplished, for from among them came those who became believers, and the blood of Christ was given to them. Their hands were guilty and red with the shedding of the blood of Christ. Those who shed His blood, He washed. Those who persecuted His mortal body which they saw became themselves His body, that is, the Church. They shed their ransom, that they might drink of it, and afterward they turned to faith in Him.
St. Augustine

entries.section: 5. The truthful Jerusalem:

paragraphs.text: The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies; neither shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth: for they shall feed and lie down, and none shall make them afraid. [13]

This holy remnant that accepts faith in the Lord Christ is marked by surpassing traits: humility accompanied by practical faith [12], holiness of conduct and not doing iniquity, and speaking the truth and not speaking lies [13]. Deceit has no place in their hearts, nor in their conduct, nor in their mouths! They are sincere in their thoughts, their works and their words, truthful in everything.

entries.section: 6. The rejoicing Jerusalem:

paragraphs.text: Sing, O daughter of Zion; shout, O Israel.
Be glad and rejoice with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem. [14]

As for the fruit of humility linked with living faith, and holiness in thought, deed and word, it is true inner joy. The Church has no work but constant thanksgiving to God, praise, shouting and unceasing gladness. It is joy “with all the heart,” in which the source of joy dwells and leaves no place in it for another.

* “O sing unto the LORD a new song” (Ps 96:1). The old man is demolished and the new man is built, therefore a new song is sung. “Sing unto the LORD, all the earth” (Ps 96:1). The earth that has turned with all its heart to the Lord sings continually songs of thanksgiving with the sweetness of a youthful voice.

* “And the heavens shall praise thy wonders, O LORD” (Ps 89:5)… If it is said to the sinner: “Thou art dust, and unto dust shalt thou return” (Gen 19:3), why is it not said to the saint or the righteous: “You are heaven, and to heaven you shall return”? For the saints, like the Apostles, [have their citizenship in heaven] (cf. Phil 3:20). Thus “the heavens shall praise thy wonders” prophesies of the repentance preached by the Apostles, by which we receive the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ. For if we obey their counsel and follow their example, we also are called “heaven,” as we imitate those who have their citizenship there… Paradise is the homeland of the saints!

St. Jerome * “Rejoice in the LORD, O ye righteous” (cf. Ps 33:1). Rejoice, O righteous, not in yourselves, for there is no safety in this, but rejoice in the Lord. “Praise is comely for the upright” (Ps 33:1). These praise the Lord, as they submit to Him, otherwise they turn aside and go astray. “Praise the LORD with harp” (Ps 33:2). Praise the Lord, presenting to Him “your bodies a living sacrifice” (Rom 12:1). “Sing unto him with the psaltery and an instrument of ten strings” (Ps 33:2). Let your members be servants of the love of God and the love of your neighbor… “Sing unto him a new song” (Ps 33:3); sing to Him a song of the grace of faith. “Play skilfully with a loud noise” (Ps 33:3); sing to Him with skill and with joy.
St. Augustine

entries.section: 7. Jerusalem the dwelling of the Lord:

paragraphs.text: 15 The LORD hath taken away thy judgments, he hath cast out thine enemy: the king of Israel, even the LORD, is in the midst of thee: thou shalt not see evil any more. 16 In that day it shall be said to Jerusalem, Fear thou not: and to Zion, Let not thine hands be slack. 17 The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.
The LORD hath taken away thy judgments.
He hath cast out thine enemy.
The king of Israel, even the LORD, is in the midst of thee.
Thou shalt not see evil any more. [15]

The secret of the Church’s joy is that He has taken away the judgments from her and struck her cases from the list, and she is no longer an object of accusation; for the Holy Righteous One took her place and accepted the sentence of death on her behalf, taking what was hers and giving her what was His, as the holy righteous Son.

The enemy, the devil, who occupied the seat of command over mankind and became the ruler of this world, no longer has a place in the true Church of Christ. The Lord removed the enemy and made a public spectacle of him by the Cross, and reigned in her midst, so that her constitution became His righteousness and holiness, and evil cannot storm her.

* May you live, O Jerusalem, in complete joy, living in perfect happiness and in satisfaction, for the Lord has taken away all your evil works and saved you from the power of your enemy, him to whom you were subject, paying the penalty of punishment. Now the Lord is in your midst, revealing His Kingdom by His care for you, so that that disturbance can no longer approach you.

Theodore of Mopsuestia * As we occupy ourselves with the deeper meaning of the passage, it clearly commands Jerusalem to rejoice exultantly, to be especially happy, and to be glad with all the heart, as her transgressions are blotted out by Christ. The holy spiritual Zion, that is, the Church, the holy assembly of believers, are justified in Christ, and in Him alone. By Him and through Him they are saved, as they escape the harm of the invisible enemies, for we have the Mediator who was incarnate and took our form, the King of all, that is, the Word of God the Father. Thanks be to Him, for we no longer see evil any more, as we are saved from the powers of evil. He (the Word) is the shield of good will, and peace, and the fortress that gives incorruption, the mediator of crowns, who nullifies the warfare of the incorporeal Assyrians and frustrates the plans of the demons.

St. Cyril of Alexandria * I know that some interpreters understand this passage of the return from Babylon and the renewal of Jerusalem, and I do not oppose these words of theirs. For the text applies also to what happened at that time. But you can find a more precise result, relating especially to the incarnation of our Savior. For He healed the brokenhearted by the washing of the new birth, as He renewed human nature, declaring His love for us, as He gave Himself for us. For “greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends” (Jn 15:13). And also “God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.”
Theodoret of Cyrus * We are at war against Satan for a time, and then we need a dwelling in which we may be refreshed.
St. Augustine

entries.section: 7. Jerusalem the dwelling of the Lord:

paragraphs.text: In that day it shall be said to Jerusalem.
Fear thou not, O Zion.
Let not thine hands be slack. [16]

As the Lord dwells in the midst of His people and dwells in the heart of the believer, He asks for the lifting up of pure hands, without slackness and without fear. For as the enemy of good vanishes and his works are scattered, so that they have no place in the Church of Christ, the Church lifts her hands in boldness and asks boldly on behalf of her children as well as for all mankind.
As for the secret of her fearlessness, it is the freedom of the glory of the children of God that she has enjoyed, so that she speaks with Him as a son or daughter with her father, without fear.

* “The LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?” (Ps 27:1). The Lord repels all attacks and thwarts all the nets of my enemy, so I fear no man. “When the wicked came upon me to eat up my flesh” (Ps 27:2), no. While the evildoers draw near to me to get to know me and harm me, so that they may be arrogant against me, I am changed to what is better. Even with their attacking teeth they will not destroy me, but will destroy my carnal desires.
St. Augustine

entries.section: 7. Jerusalem the dwelling of the Lord:

paragraphs.text: The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save.
He will rejoice over thee with joy.
He will rest in his love.
He will joy over thee with singing. [17]
As the remnant returns to the Lord, the Lord ascribes Himself to it, glorying in it, and so it is said to her “thy God,” as it is said: “the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob.”

He is in the midst of His Church, the Almighty God, able to save to the uttermost. He defends her and grants her the life of victory. This is the object of His gladness and joy in His love for her, and He contemplates her spiritual beauty like one who is silent, not in ignoring her, but in His great love toward her. He rests in His love for her.

How wonderful, for we know that God is the source of our gladness, exultation and happiness, but to hear of God that He rejoices and is pleased with us, in this we see a wonder! Truly, as the son of Sirach says, “the delight of God is in the sons of men,” and as the Lord Christ Himself says, “there shall be joy in heaven over one sinner that repenteth” (Lk 15). He is the Father who rejoices in embracing His children and bestowing heavenly glories upon them.

* Surely He will save, but He will do this according to the manner in which He promised. But in what manner did He promise? That we desire salvation and that we listen to Him. For He makes no promise to wooden planks.
St. John Chrysostom

entries.section: 8. Jerusalem enjoying salvation:

paragraphs.text: 18 I will gather them that are sorrowful for the solemn assembly, who are of thee, to whom the reproach of it was a burden. 19 Behold, at that time I will undo all that afflict thee: and I will save her that halteth, and gather her that was driven out; and I will get them praise and fame in every land where they have been put to shame.
Who are of thee, to whom the reproach of it was a burden. [18]

Sorrow reigned over the hearts of the captives, so they refused to sing with the harps. As the psalmist says: “By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion. We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’s song in a strange land? If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand be forgotten…” (Ps 137). But now that the Lord has turned back the captivity and brought them into the spiritual Jerusalem, and they have the freedom of the children of God, their whole being has become a spiritual harp on which the Holy Spirit of God plays songs of salvation, thanksgiving and praise. Her reproach is gone, her sorrow is scattered, and she bears an inner glory and a surpassing heavenly joy.

entries.section: 8. Jerusalem enjoying salvation:

paragraphs.text: Behold, at that time I will undo all that afflict thee: and I will save her that halteth, and gather her that was driven out; and I will get them praise and fame in every land where they have been put to shame. [19]

As the holy remnant enjoys salvation from the captivity of the devil and his reproach, her weakness does not stand as an obstacle on the path of her true glory. For the Savior who dwells in her deals with the one who had previously humiliated her, removing his authority over her and breaking his tyranny and power.
If the enemy has made her lame, unable to move, the Savior moves on her behalf, so that she no longer feels weakness and helplessness.
And if the enemy has taken her captive and exiled her and scattered her far from her homeland, the Savior gathers her from exile and brings her in as to her heavenly home.
And if the enemy has disfigured her image and poured upon her reproach and shame, she bears the name of her Savior in all the earth and herself becomes His praise, a source of joy to many.

entries.section: 9. The glorious Jerusalem:

paragraphs.text: At that time will I bring you again, even in the time that I gather you.
For I will make you a name and a praise among all people of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before your eyes, saith the LORD. [20]

He concludes the book with the announcement of the Church of the New Testament as a glorious Church, reflecting within her the radiance of the glory of her heavenly Bridegroom. She who was formerly an object of mockery and derision, now her name is among all the peoples of the earth, a source of joy for all mankind. All marvel in amazement how the captive became free, and she who was in shame has come into surpassing glory!

* The salvation of mankind is accomplished by the tenderness of God alone. We do not obtain it as wages for our righteousness, but rather it is a gift and divine goodness. Therefore the Lord says: “For your sake I will save and quicken,” and I will bring back to Myself what had become another’s, and make him prominent, more renowned than others, and free him from the former reproach and from his captivity and bondage. I will make them a free people for Me. Now, as I said, He made both a gift: to those who returned from Babylon at that time, and what He afterward gave to all the people. We who were formerly enslaved to Satan have now become free from that violent bondage, and those who had fallen without reason into the worship of many gods have become God’s; they have become more renowned than the pagans and the barbarians according to the prophecy. And we who were formerly far off have become near, as the divine Apostle said.

Theodoret of Cyrus As the believer enjoys salvation, God rejoices in him as an object of His delight, and this is reflected on all those whom the believer meets, so that he becomes a source of joy to many, as they come into contact with the Lord Christ who dwells in him, the fountain of joy. His very name becomes a song of praise that people sing.

Wherever the true believer settles he turns the place as into a heaven, by the grace of God working in him. And what we say of the believer we say of the Church as a whole, whose name turns into a song of praise that many call blessed, as a source of joy and exultation for them.

This is the experience of St. Mary, who bore her Savior in her womb, and became a song of praise among all the peoples of the earth, as she said: “from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed.”
You demolish and You build!
* I entrust no hand with my demolition but Your divine hand; it demolishes and builds!
You demolish my rebellion, my uncleanness and my injustice; You remove all ingratitude within me.
You scatter all arrogance that has crept into my depths; You kill every wolfish, predatory thought.
* Instead of my dryness You grant me the spirit of living worship, so that the river of Your Holy Spirit flows within me, turning my wasteland into a garden and a paradise.
He grants me fellowship in the divine nature.
I find my delight in enjoying obedience, humility and gentleness.
I bear Your obedience, I enjoy Your humility and I delight in Your gentleness.
Glory to You, who work in sinners, and grant Your servants Your righteousness that they may hide in it.

* Your wonderful Spirit raises from me a rejoicing Jerusalem, and turns my depths into the temple of Your sanctuary, so that I become a dwelling for You, knowing only the joy of heaven and the exultation of the angels!
I enjoy Your salvation and delight in the earnest of the glory of eternity.
Glory to You, who give glory to those who love You!
